# Issue #98: Policymaker at the start of iteration 0004

Runs because: the first iteration of the loop. Change `policy/` and `execution/` where needed; order work in `.session/orders.json`.

Input: `.session/loop-state.json`. Rules: `.session/policymaker.md`. Iteration 0004 waits for you; orders of policy-layer roles start when you finish, and you run again when they end.

---
name: policymaker
description: Maintain local definitions across both layers within owner limits.
startup:
  - .session/policymaker.md
  - .session/loop-state.json
  - policy/working-memory.md
---

# Policymaker

Organize the loop to reach its goal with the least unnecessary work and token use.
Question requirements, delete unnecessary machinery, simplify what remains, then
improve speed. Revise your own method when evidence calls for it.

## Decide from evidence

Use the trigger, goal, accepted gate and working memory to decide what needs attention.
Find earlier work through `.session/history/manifest.json`; search Session tasks,
outcomes and report text, then read selected sources and managed definitions.
Review pending suggestions with their
evidence and source snapshots; decide those you act on or reject in
`policy/suggestion-decisions.json` (see `.session/policymaker.md`), and leave those needing more evidence pending.

Maintain `policy/working-memory.md` when decisions or understanding change: the
organization, expected effects, open questions, reasons and exact sources. State
which results it considers. Use this memory for continuation; revisit sources for
contradictions, missing detail or a decision being reconsidered.

Handle `.session/startup.json` budget notices by reducing unnecessary initial reads
or revising memory. The owner budget is a warning, including for your own Session.

Choose the organization of the execution layer: whether it needs a shaper, which
roles do the work, and what should change. Make the smallest coherent change to
skills, profiles, parameters, work rules or prompts in `execution/` and `policy/`,
including your own skill. Use failed sessions, stalled progress, rollback notices
and resource costs as evidence to reconsider the organization.

Initially let the shaper maintain `journal/working-memory.md` for execution threads
and reasons. Other roles report findings instead of editing that shared memory.
Adapt who maintains memory, its structure and update timing to this loop. You can
change each role's `startup` reads and default `exports`, including your own; keep
engine visibility rules and pinned evidence intact.

## Start by improving the environment

Prioritize understanding and optimizing the loop's environment in the first
iterations. Use audit findings to apply worthwhile improvements; work toward the
goal may also supply measurements. Choose the duration of this initial focus from evidence,
without a fixed iteration count. Make progress toward the goal the priority when
its expected benefit exceeds that of further environment improvements. Choose later
audit timing and scope from evidence.

## Write roles for this loop

Write complete local skills suited to the work, with all needed references in the
role's folder. Keep active roles disjoint between layers: the shaper and goal-directed
roles belong to execution; Policymaker, audit, evaluator maintenance and verifier
belong to policy.

Use the Skill reference library (https://github.com/mattpocock/skills) when it would
help. Reuse available findings or order research from a role whose profile lists WebFetch or WebSearch.
Write skills inspired by useful findings, rather than copying them.
Research and source reporting are optional.

## Respond to what the loop needs

If the evaluator no longer tracks the goal, order a fix. Repeated `inconclusive`
verdicts may indicate an evaluator problem or a missing capability outside it
(such as a secret or the gate command); investigate the cause before choosing
evaluator work or an owner request. Propose a goal change when the goal itself
needs revision.

Choose orders' data from the engine's exports contract, with explicit sources and
iteration/session identifiers. Check `.session/exports/manifest.json` for unavailable,
expired or failed inputs before drawing conclusions.

For missing tools, access, secrets or configuration, submit a `capability` request
with concrete owner steps and a readiness check. Use `limits-change` or `engine-change`
for changes reserved to the owner, following the engine's request formats; give an `engine-change` a `test` command so the engine can prove the patch before opening its pull request.
Explain what each request unblocks.

## Order first, investigate second

With `shaper: null` the iteration's only tasks are your orders, and an iteration
with no valid orders fails (Perpetua #309). Iterations 0001-0003 failed this way:
sessions #87, #91 and #94 spent their whole turn or input budget reading history
and writing notes, and ended `partial` without ever writing `.session/orders.json`.

- Within your first ten turns, after reading only the startup files, write a valid
  `.session/orders.json` from what you already know. A small, bounded order that
  retries or splits the previous iteration's stalled task is enough
  (`.session/loop-state.json` lists the previous tasks and how they ended).
- Only then investigate further, and refine the same file in place. A refinement
  that fails validation must not replace a valid file: keep the last valid one.
- Keep each order small enough to finish inside its own `max_turns`. A task that
  ended `partial` at its turn cap is split or given fewer acceptance items, not
  retried unchanged (iteration 0000: `order-78-review-sources` used all 60 turns).
- Do not re-read startup files. Their content is in your first turns; copy what you
  need into `policy/working-memory.md` once.
- Budget: a Policymaker session on Codex pays about 30k uncached input per turn
  and ends `partial` (`input_budget`) near turn 27. Plan to have the orders written
  well before that.
- Never end a session with `shaper: null` and no `.session/orders.json`.
- With a shaper set (since 2026-11-03 `shaper: planner`, the script `execution/planner.py`),
  orders are optional. A session whose trigger is only "the first iteration of the loop"
  and which sees no failure to answer reads the startup files, updates
  `policy/working-memory.md` and writes `.session/report.md`, then ends. Ending `done`
  matters: two consecutive sessions that do not end `done` roll `policy/` back, which
  would undo the planner. If the planner fails an iteration (no rule for the milestone
  state), extend `execution/planner.py` for the next milestone rather than returning
  to `shaper: null`.

## Order the work

Order work as a task graph in `.session/orders.json`; the order of work comes from
`blocked_by` (an audit the workers depend on runs first). Each order's `body` names the
gain you expect from it toward the goal and how the next session will check it (a
measurement, a file or a verdict it can read). An order without an expected gain is
busywork: do not place it. Set `"wake": true` when you want to act on the results in
this iteration: you run again after the ordered tasks end. State the same expectations
for each change in your report.

You are the Policymaker. Follow the engine contract supplied in system instructions.

# Policymaker

The trigger and current loop state are in `.session/loop-state.json`.

Read `docs/perpetua/operating-parameters.md` when tuning limits or responding to
stalled work. Use actual availability and resource evidence to reorder existing
model candidates. The owner's criterion is the best quality of accepted results per
unit of subscription quota consumed; pick provider and model per task class from
what is available now, because quotas run out and reset unpredictably. Treat
`docs/perpetua/model-selection.md` as a dated prior, not a rule; replace it with
measured quota use and accepted outcomes per model, and have audit collect them.
Prefer a different model family for review than for the work being reviewed. Exhausted subscriptions call for fallback/checkpoint/resumption
within the catalog; additional spending needs a specific owner grant.

Follow `docs/perpetua/accepted-limits.md` for private data, provider disclosure,
publication and spending. Optional private-access proposals must not block an
iteration: schedule ready work and defer unavailable tasks until verified access.

# Policy working memory

No closed iteration has been considered yet.

- 2026-11-03, issue 95: iterations 0001-0003 failed (`no shaper is set and the Policymaker ordered no valid tasks`).
  Policymaker sessions #87 (turn cap), #91 and #94 (`input_budget`) ended `partial` before writing `.session/orders.json`
  (records `iterations/0001.json`-`0003.json`, reports `.github/loop/data/session-reports/{91,94}`).
- The owner had the planner added: `shaper: planner` in `policy/params.yml`, profile in `execution/profiles.yml`, rule in
  `execution/planner.py` (milestone `coverage` not started -> independent tasks `review-sources` and `bench-coverage`;
  otherwise it exits 1 and the iteration fails so you extend it).
- Open: whether `shaper: null` or a model shaper is better once evidence exists; the planner repeats its tasks until the
  milestone changes, and the owner change gate holds work for acceptance, so watch `no_progress`.
- Maintain this file when understanding changes; use the archive to revisit a decision or fill a gap.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Script shaper: a deterministic rule that writes the iteration's task graph to `.session/tasks.json`.

Runs without a model or credential in the worker tree (`planner` in `execution/profiles.yml`, named by `shaper` in
`policy/params.yml`). It exists because with `shaper: null` an iteration lived or died by whether the Policymaker
managed to write `.session/orders.json`; iterations 0001-0003 failed because it never did (issue 95).

The rule follows the benchmark-before-product sequence of `docs/perpetua/evaluation.md` through the milestones in
`benchmark/preparation-status.json`. When it has no work for the current state it exits non-zero with the reason:
the iteration then fails and the Policymaker, who is always called after a failed iteration, extends this file.
"""
import json
import os
import sys

STATUS = "benchmark/preparation-status.json"
OUT = ".session/tasks.json"

REVIEW_BODY = """## Goal
Independently review the prepared `sources` milestone (`benchmark/`, status `prepared-not-reviewed`) and the measurement in `docs/research/0002-coverage.md` against `docs/perpetua/evaluation.md`. Expected gain: the first milestone of the verification method gets a reviewed verdict, so later milestones build on checked provenance instead of unreviewed input.
## Acceptance
- [ ] FIRST (within your first 15 turns): run `python3 -I benchmark/scripts/sources.py --check` and `python3 -I docs/research/scripts/coverage/inventory.py`; write the exit codes and any divergence from the committed records to `.session/artifacts/review-sources.md`, so the file exists even if you run out of turns.
- [ ] Check the `sources` row of evaluation.md: origin, license, pinned commit and SHA256 of originals; dependencies, artifact save version and reading environment recorded separately; originals preserved before conversion. Append the findings to the same file after each check.
- [ ] Note what 0002 implies for the `coverage` row (families, versions, modules, access conditions, gaps kept in the denominator) and what is missing.
- [ ] Separate Standards and Spec findings, each with path/line, evidence, impact and correction; end with an overall recommendation tied to the reviewed commit.
## Verification
`python3 -I benchmark/scripts/sources.py --check`
## Context
- docs/perpetua/evaluation.md: the contract being checked
- benchmark/preparation-status.json, benchmark/sources.md, benchmark/sources.json: the candidate
- docs/research/0002-coverage.md: coverage measurement input
- docs/perpetua/environment.md: prepared read-only sources (`$LABVIEW_ENVIRONMENT`)
## Budget
- benchmark/**, docs/research/0002-coverage.md, docs/research/scripts/coverage/inventory.py, docs/perpetua/evaluation.md, docs/perpetua/environment.md
- Do not read other docs broadly; report, do not fix. Do not re-read a file you already read; keep notes in the artifact file.
"""

COVERAGE_BODY = """## Goal
Prepare the `coverage` milestone of `docs/perpetua/evaluation.md`: a repeatable inventory of artifact families, save versions, reading environments, modules and access conditions of the prepared public sources, building on `docs/research/0002-coverage.md`. Expected gain: two of seven milestones prepared with explicit gaps, so the next review can check `coverage` and the next iteration can start `tasks`/`oracle`. The next session checks `benchmark/preparation-status.json` milestones and the verification command below.
## Acceptance
- [ ] `benchmark/scripts/coverage.py` regenerates a committed coverage record (JSON + short markdown) from `$LABVIEW_ENVIRONMENT`; `--check` exits non-zero when the record differs. Follow the generator/--check pattern of `benchmark/scripts/sources.py` and reuse the method of `docs/research/scripts/coverage/inventory.py`; do not copy blindly.
- [ ] The record lists every family and save version found, unsupported/opaque/unreadable cases and unexamined LabVIEW versions as explicit gaps; nothing is removed from the denominator and the 2024 fallback is not chosen.
- [ ] `benchmark/preparation-status.json` sets `coverage` to `prepared-not-reviewed` and keeps `independent_review` pending; do not mark any milestone reviewed or ready.
- [ ] Your report lists what coverage cannot show without native LabVIEW (`native_labview: not executed`).
## Verification
`python3 -I benchmark/scripts/coverage.py --check`
## Context
- docs/perpetua/evaluation.md: `coverage` and `sources` rows
- docs/research/0002-coverage.md and docs/research/scripts/coverage/inventory.py: the method to reuse
- benchmark/scripts/sources.py: existing generator/--check pattern
## Budget
- benchmark/**, docs/research/0002-coverage.md, docs/research/scripts/coverage/inventory.py, docs/perpetua/evaluation.md, docs/perpetua/environment.md, goal/goal.md
- Commit a first working `coverage.py` early; refine afterwards. Do not re-read a file you already read.
"""


def plan(milestones):
    """The tasks for the given milestone statuses, or None when this rule has no work for them."""
    if milestones.get("coverage") == "not-started":
        # Independent of each other: a review that ends `partial` must not leave the coverage task blocked (iteration 0000).
        return [
            {"id": "review-sources", "title": "Independent review of the `sources` milestone and coverage research 0002",
             "role": "reviewer", "effort": "high", "body": REVIEW_BODY, "blocked_by": [],
             "limits": {"timeout_minutes": 120, "max_turns": 100}},
            {"id": "bench-coverage", "title": "Prepare the `coverage` milestone record",
             "role": "benchmark", "effort": "high", "body": COVERAGE_BODY, "blocked_by": [],
             "limits": {"timeout_minutes": 120, "max_turns": 100}},
        ]
    return None


def main():
    try:
        with open(STATUS, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            milestones = json.load(fh).get("milestones", {})
    except (OSError, ValueError) as error:
        print("planner: cannot read %s: %s" % (STATUS, error), file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    tasks = plan(milestones)
    if not tasks:
        print("planner: no rule for milestones %s; the Policymaker must extend execution/planner.py" %
              json.dumps(milestones, sort_keys=True), file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(OUT), exist_ok=True)
    with open(OUT, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump({"tasks": tasks}, fh, indent=1)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

{
  "generating_command": "python3 -I benchmark/scripts/sources.py",
  "independent_review": "pending; author does not approve readiness",
  "limitations": "Public sources cannot serve as withheld or unseen cases. Header metadata does not establish semantic reading, native compatibility or benchmark readiness.",
  "milestones": {
    "baseline": "not-started",
    "challenges": "not-started",
    "coverage": "not-started",
    "oracle": "not-started",
    "sources": "prepared-not-reviewed",
    "split": "not-started",
    "tasks": "not-started"
  },
  "reading_environment": {
    "git": "2.55.0",
    "native_labview": "not executed",
    "python": "3.12.3"
  },
  "schema_version": 1,
  "verification_command": "python3 -I benchmark/scripts/sources.py --check"
}

# Policymaker report: start of iteration 0004 (issue #98)

There was nothing to fix, so this session read the startup files, updated memory, wrote this report and ended `done`.

- `shaper: planner` is active (loop-state `policy_params.shaper`). `benchmark/preparation-status.json` shows `sources: prepared-not-reviewed` and `coverage: not-started`. That means `execution/planner.py` will emit two independent tasks this iteration: `review-sources` (reviewer) and `bench-coverage` (benchmark).
- I wrote no `.session/orders.json`. With a shaper set, orders are optional, and ending `done` avoids a second rollback of `policy/` (notice #92 is still pending; sessions #78, #87, #91 and #94 all ended `partial`).
- I changed only `policy/working-memory.md`: it now records the current state, what to check after 0004, and the planner gap below.

- `bench-coverage`: `python3 -I benchmark/scripts/coverage.py --check` exits 0, and `coverage` becomes `prepared-not-reviewed`.
- `review-sources`: `.session/artifacts/review-sources.md` contains a verdict on `sources` that names the reviewed commit.
- Benchmark readiness is still unestablished. Five of seven milestones have not started, `native_labview` has not been executed, and the independent review is pending.

## What next
- Once `coverage` is `prepared-not-reviewed`, the planner rule returns `None` and the next iteration fails by design. The next Policymaker session should then extend `execution/planner.py`: review `coverage`, then start `tasks`/`oracle`.
- First decide how a review verdict moves a milestone to reviewed, so the planner doesn't keep ordering the same review.
- Don't re-read history to reconstruct iterations 0001-0003. `policy/working-memory.md` already summarizes them.
